correctness.rationale: Exact prior unit-disk arc area formula independently reconstructed as a product-to-sum cosine difference. The derivative comparison uses strict monotonicity of x cot x to prove unique P=π maximum for every integer m≥3. The exact quadratic remainder is E_{π/2}(|s|)-m E_{π/m}(|s|)/(2 sin(π/m)); a two-term alternating Taylor bound combined with sin(π/m)≥2/m shows this is strictly positive for 0<|s|<1, and zero at |s|=0 or 1. Endpoint equality certifies optimality of G_m/π². Independent radial integration and symbolic checks in verify.py match the formulas; finite checks are not infinite proof. Degenerate endpoints and strict interior quantifiers are explicitly separated.

value.rationale: A natural geometric gap measures how much more area a regularly faceted unit-ball intersection encloses than the universal equal-perimeter lens lower benchmark. Its sharp maximum and optimal stability rate are intrinsic optimization invariants, not arbitrary parameter slices. The new result identifies a common half-perimeter extremizer for every number of disks, sharp m-dependent gap constants and global quantitative stability with equality at the two degeneracies, supplying exact test cases for curvature-constrained stability and regular disk-polygon approximation. It is an exact finite-parameter-family classification rather than a broad all-configurations theorem.
